newsitem.title: UK: Trinidad and Tobago to quit coffee pact.
newsitem.headline: Trinidad and Tobago to quit coffee pact.

text.p: Trinidad and Tobago will quit the International Coffee Agreement from June 25 while Benin and Ghana may rejoin the producer-consumer accord, the International Coffee Organisation (ICO) said.

Trinidad and Tobago's pull-out following the country's shrinking coffee sector will bring the number of member nations down to 61, ICO spokesman Pablo Dubois told reporters at the week-long ICO talks.
The London-based ICO administers the global coffee agreement.
The ICO executive board, which comprises 16 producer and consumer nations, is expected to wrap up its talks by Thursday before the full council meets later on Thursday and Friday.
Dubois said the ICO would continue talks on the proposal to revise the group's indicator prices to bring them in line with current market trends.
"There's no real consensus yet on the proposal," he said. The issue is likely to be further examined by a technical working group, he said.
Dubois said the current 50/50 weighting split between robusta and arabica prices used in the ICO indicator price could be reviewed.
Also, the 75:25 weighting for the Other Milds group, based on U.S. and Germany prices, which are now in U.S. favour, could be reviewed to reflect higher German weighting, he said.
The current weighting for the latter was based on trade pattern in the mid-1970s.
